subject: maths
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: A translation is fully described by which of the following?
options: The equation of a mirror line
questions.explain: A translation moves every point the same distance in the same direction, described by a column vector giving the horizontal and vertical shift.

questions.q: Which of the four transformations changes the size of an object?
questions.explain: An enlargement scales the object by its scale factor, so it is the only one that can change size.

questions.q: To fully describe a rotation you must state the centre of rotation, and which two other pieces of information?
options: A scale factor and a direction
A mirror line and an angle
A column vector and an angle
questions.explain: A rotation needs a centre, an angle and a direction (clockwise or anticlockwise) to be uniquely defined.

questions.q: What single piece of information is needed to fully describe a reflection?
options: The equation of the mirror line
questions.explain: A reflection is defined entirely by its mirror line, given as the equation of that line.

questions.q: In a column vector, what does the top number represent?
questions.explain: In a column vector the top component gives the movement in the x-direction and the bottom component the movement in the y-direction.

questions.q: For a vector with components x and y, its magnitude is given by which formula?
questions.explain: The magnitude (length) of a vector is found using Pythagoras' theorem as √(x² + y²).

questions.q: To fully describe an enlargement you must state the scale factor and which other piece of information?
questions.explain: An enlargement is defined by its centre of enlargement together with its scale factor.

questions.q: Two vectors are parallel if and only if one is which of the following of the other?
questions.explain: Vectors are parallel exactly when one can be written as a scalar multiple of the other.

questions.q: An object is enlarged by a scale factor k where 0 < k < 1. What happens to the image?
options: It becomes smaller than the object
It becomes larger than the object
It stays the same size but rotates
questions.explain: A positive scale factor between 0 and 1 reduces the size, producing a smaller image.

questions.q: An object is enlarged by a negative scale factor about a centre. Where does the image appear?
options: On the opposite side of the centre, inverted
On the same side of the centre, the same way up
Reflected in a vertical mirror line
questions.explain: A negative scale factor places the image on the opposite side of the centre and turns it upside down.

questions.q: Which transformation does NOT generally produce an image congruent to the original object?
questions.explain: Reflections, rotations and translations preserve size and shape, but an enlargement changes the size (unless the scale factor is ±1).

questions.q: Given the vector a = (3, -1), what is 2a as a column vector?
questions.explain: Multiplying a vector by a scalar multiplies each component, so 2a = (2×3, 2×-1) = (6, -2).

questions.q: If a = (2, 5) and b = (-3, 1), what is a + b?
questions.explain: Vectors are added by adding corresponding components: (2 + -3, 5 + 1) = (-1, 6).

questions.q: What is the magnitude of the vector (0, -7)?
questions.explain: The magnitude is √(0² + (-7)²) = √49 = 7; magnitude is always non-negative.

questions.q: Points A, B and C satisfy vector AB = 2 vector BC. Since these vectors are parallel and share point B, what can be concluded?
options: A, B and C are collinear
B is the midpoint of AC
questions.explain: Parallel vectors that share a common point lie on the same straight line, so the three points are collinear.

questions.q: If a is a vector, how does the vector -a compare to a?
questions.explain: Negating a vector reverses its direction while keeping its length unchanged.

questions.q: The point (2, 3) is reflected in the x-axis. What are the coordinates of its image?
questions.explain: Reflection in the x-axis keeps the x-coordinate and changes the sign of the y-coordinate, giving (2, -3).

questions.q: The point (4, 1) is translated by the column vector (-3, 2). What is the image point?
questions.explain: Add the vector components to the coordinates: (4 + -3, 1 + 2) = (1, 3).

questions.q: What is the magnitude of the vector (3, 4)?
questions.explain: The magnitude is √(3² + 4²) = √25 = 5.

questions.q: What is the magnitude of the vector (5, 12)?
questions.explain: The magnitude is √(5² + 12²) = √169 = 13.

specSource: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics (0580) syllabus; Transformations & Vectors
